questions.question: Write a difference between unary and binary operator.
questions.solution: A unary operator works on a single operand, e.g. ++a, -a, !flag. A binary operator works on two operands, e.g. a + b, a > b, a && b.

marking_points.point: Unary operator acts on one operand, with example

questions.question: Differentiate between if else if and switch-case statements.
questions.solution: if-else-if can test any type of condition (relational/logical expressions, ranges, any data type), whereas switch-case tests only equality of a single expression against constant case values (int, char, String etc.). In if-else-if, once a condition is true the remaining conditions are skipped automatically, whereas in switch a missing break causes fall through to the next case.

marking_points.point: if-else-if evaluates any relational/logical condition (ranges, any type)
switch-case checks only equality of one expression against constant case labels

questions.question: What are the various types of errors in Java?
questions.solution: (1) Syntax (compile-time) errors: violation of the rules of the language, e.g. missing semicolon. (2) Runtime errors: occur during execution, e.g. division by zero, array index out of bounds. (3) Logical errors: the program runs but gives wrong output because of faulty logic, e.g. using + instead of *.

marking_points.point: Syntax / compile-time errors named and explained
Runtime errors named and explained
Logical errors named and explained

questions.question: What is the difference between the linear search and the binary search technique?
questions.solution: Linear search compares the search value with each element one by one from the beginning; the array need not be sorted. Binary search works only on a sorted array: it compares with the middle element and repeatedly halves the search range, so it is much faster for large arrays.

marking_points.point: Linear search: element-by-element comparison, works on unsorted array
Binary search: needs sorted array, repeatedly compares middle element and halves the range

questions.topic: Call by value vs call by reference
questions.question: State a difference between call by value and call by reference.
questions.solution: In call by value, a copy of the actual parameter's value is passed (primitive types), so changes made to the formal parameter inside the method do not affect the actual parameter. In call by reference, the reference (address) of the object/array is passed, so changes made inside the method are reflected in the original.

marking_points.point: Call by value: copy passed, original unchanged
Call by reference: reference passed, changes reflected in original

questions.question:
Evaluate the following expression if the value of x=2, y=3 and z=1.
v=x+ --z+ y++ +y
questions.solution: v = x + (--z) + (y++) + y = 2 + 0 + 3 + 4 = 9. (--z makes z 0 before use; y++ uses 3 then makes y 4; the last y is 4.)

(i) Big data (index 3 is the fourth element)
(ii) 4

questions.topic: Class with constructor and discount slabs (ShowRoom)
questions.question:
Design a class name ShowRoom with the following description:
Instance variables / Data members:
String name - To store the name of the customer
long mobno - To store the mobile number of the customer
double cost - To store the cost of the items purchased
double dis - To store the discount amount
double amount - To store the amount to be paid after discount
Member methods:
ShowRoom( ) - default constructor to initialize data members
void input( ) - To input customer name, mobile number, cost
void calculate( ) - To calculate discount on the cost of purchased items, based on following criteria
Cost | Discount (in percentage)
Less than or equal to ₹ 10000 | 5%
More than ₹ 10000 and less than or equal to ₹ 20000 | 10%
More than ₹ 20000 and less than or equal to ₹ 35000 | 15%
More than ₹ 35000 | 20%
void display( ) - To display customer name, mobile number, amount to be paid after discount.
Write a main method to create an object of the class and call the above member methods.

marking_points.point: Class declaration with the five data members of correct types
Default constructor initialising all data members
input() using Scanner for name, mobile number (long) and cost
calculate(): correct if-else-if slabs 5%/10%/15%/20% with correct boundaries
amount = cost - dis
display() prints name, mobile number and amount
main() creates object and calls input, calculate, display
